title: To provide for the extension of the enforcement instruction on supervision requirements for outpatient therapeutic services in critical access and small rural hospitals through 2014.
official_summary:
(This measure has not been amended since it was introduced. The summary of that version is repeated here.)

Requires the Secretary of Health and Human Services (HHS) to continue to instruct Medicare contractors not to enforce requirements for direct physician supervision of outpatient therapeutic services in critical access and small rural hospitals through 2014.

summary.headline: A 2014 law tells Medicare contractors to keep not enforcing a physician supervision rule for certain therapy services at small rural and critical access hospitals through 2014.
summary.what_it_does: The law requires the Secretary of Health and Human Services to continue instructing Medicare contractors not to enforce direct physician supervision requirements for outpatient therapeutic services. It applies to critical access hospitals and small rural hospitals. The extension runs only through the end of 2014.

who_it_affects.how: They keep the temporary relief from direct physician supervision requirements for outpatient therapy services through 2014.
They keep the same temporary relief from direct physician supervision requirements for outpatient therapy services through 2014.

who_it_affects.group: Medicare patients receiving outpatient therapy at these hospitals
who_it_affects.how: Services they receive at these hospitals during this period are not held to the direct physician supervision enforcement rule.

summary.when_it_takes_effect: Enacted December 4, 2014, and the enforcement pause covers services through 2014.
